title: WNBA gameday discussion: The latest Liberty vs. Aces matchup is a reminder that this league still belongs to Breanna Stewart and A’ja Wilson
description: Breanna Stewart and A’ja Wilson remain the queens of the WNBA.
fullText:
What remains one of the WNBA’s most compelling rivalries resumes on Thursday night in Sin City: New York Liberty vs. Las Vegas Aces (10 p.m. ET, Prime Video).

Neither team occupies the superteam heights they occupied when this rivalry first launched during the 2023 season.

Despite their status as defending champions, the Aces’ dominance is now pocked with inconsistency, largely due to their lack of depth. After failing to repeat as champs, the Liberty looked for an injection of new energy over the offseason, only to instead become beset by an athleticism deficit that has been compounded by injuries.

And yet, Liberty vs. Aces will always intrigue because for two reasons: Stewie and A’ja.

Stew’ja still are the definitional stars of this league. Their shared status only has been confirmed by their recent performances, where their teams have been as dependent as ever on their absolute brilliance in order to earn wins.

A’ja Wilson and Breanna Stewart have statistically been the WNBA’s two best players this season, and it's no surprise both have continued that dominance throughout July.

Here’s a look at their numbers this month as they prepare for a highly anticipated showdown against each… pic.twitter.com/UUuBEJoXQY

— I talk hoops 🏀 (@trendyhoopstars) July 29, 2026

After New York suffered through a four-game losing streak, Breanna Stewart seemingly decided that she would do whatever it took to lift the Liberty out of their rut.

First, she dropped a 33-point and 10-rebound double-double in a win over the Dallas Wings, playing 42 minutes in the overtime affair. Then, she battled her way to 20 points and nine boards as New York escaped against the Chicago Sky. In the Liberty’s first post-All-Star game, she filled the stat sheet for 29 points, seven assists, four rebounds, four steals and three blocks to get the win over the Los Angeles Sparks.

Increasing the lead 👏

Breanna Stewart calls her own number as she scores on consecutive possessions and forces a timeout call!

NYL-LAS | League Pass 
Tap to watch: https://t.co/sl0hN0tCOl pic.twitter.com/SlGLvSq6at

The season-long leader in wRAPM (regularized adjusted plus-minus) according to Help the Helper, as well as databallr’s RAPM calculation, Stewart has been, at least according to advanced metrics, the most impactful player in the WNBA this season.

The Liberty’s struggles have demanded that Stewie shine, and she has. And of late, her star has been even brighter.

Star power, of course, has become synonymous with A’ja Wilson.

And A’ja understands that with great power comes great responsibility, or accountability. That’s something the four-time MVP consistently expressed in ESPN’s Life in the W documentary. Last season, Wilson, despite her individual excellence, owned the Aces’ struggles, and made it her mission to fix them. Wilson’s acute understanding of the expectations that come with her indvidual achievements and accolades produced title No. 3 for the Aces.

This season, again, is asking a lot of A’ja. And she is, once again, delivering.

Amongst Vegas’ overall uneven performances of late, she is a guarantee.

In a blowout victory over the Toronto Tempo, Wilson nearly put up a point a minute, scoring 26 points in 28 minutes on über-efficiency. When the Aces fell short against the Washington Mystics in DC, she still poured in 38 points, grabbed seven boards, dished five assists, swiped three steals and swatted two shots. Out of the All-Star break, it was more of the same, with a 28-point and 14-rebound double-double in a win over the Portland Fire.

Everywhere on the floor 😮‍💨

A'ja Wilson finished with 28 PTS on 7-of-10 shooting, 14 REB, 4 AST and 2 STL in another dominant performance to power the Aces to the win!#WNBASeason30 pic.twitter.com/cKOFMjsjJG

All that production has padded A’ja’s lead at the top of ESPN Analytics’ MVP ladder, with Wilson having accumulated 123.8 net points, more than 20 points more that second place.

So, the winners of the last four WNBA MVP awards, as well as six of the last eight, deservedly take center stage on Thursday night.

For all their issues, the Liberty have enjoyed two of their best performances of the season against the Aces. Before surviving against the A’ja-less Aces to win the Commissioner’s Cup, the Liberty, powered by 15 second-half points from Stewie, secured an 11-point win in Vegas.

Will the matchup with a familiar foe again produce a favorable outcome for Stewie and the Liberty? Or, in true rivalry fashion, will A’ja and Aces reclaim the advantage?

In the comments, let us know what you expect to see from the Liberty, Aces, Stewie and A’ja, as well as the other stars involved, on Thursday night.

title: Maresca has an eye for detail, says Semenyo
description: Antoine Semenyo says City’s players are enjoying Enzo Maresca’s first couple of weeks at the helm. Men's Team I’m looking forward to seeing what Maresca achieves here, says Wright-Phillips Mares...
fullText:
Antoine Semenyo says City’s players are enjoying Enzo Maresca’s first couple of weeks at the helm.

Maresca replaced Pep Guardiola as boss earlier this summer and is approaching the end of his second week on the training ground.

After seven days at the City Football Academy, the Blues have now flown out to Hong Kong where we are preparing to face Inter in a 12:30 (UK) kick-off this Saturday.

Following that, we’ll travel on to Seoul to play a K League All Stars side and Atletico Madrid, completing preparations for the Community Shield and the Premier League season.

All three games in Asia are live on mancity.com and our official app globally for CITY+ subscribers.

Ahead of that, Semenyo says the City squad are getting to grips with Maresca’s demands.

“Very good, very detailed,” he said about the manager’s training sessions.

“He’s got an eye for detail and he wants everything to be right, which is quite similar to Pep. That’s good for us as players so we’ve enjoyed it so far.”

City were greeted into Hong Kong by a huge crowd outside the hotel and have since got to see some of the best of the city, including a spectacular floating patch in the iconic harbour.

Semenyo says seeing that support reminds the players of the passion for City all around the world.

“The club are global and have a lot of fans,” he began.

“Getting to the hotel from the airport and seeing so many people welcoming us shows the great support we have out here and we look forward to playing in front of them.”

City’s clashes with Inter and Atletico Madrid could well be a prelude to Champions League ties in the coming season and Semenyo says ties like this add an extra edge to pre-season.

“It prepares the players here for the season ahead,” said Semenyo.

“There’s a lot of tough teams in the Premier League and Champions League and Inter and Atletico are two of those so we know that playing those at this stage is a good test for us.”

Since joining City in January, Semenyo has already played 27 times for the Blues and been to the World Cup with Ghana.

However, he insists he’s ready to go as the new campaign nears.

“My body feels good. I like to think I’m well rested,” said Semenyo.

“The manager gave me a couple of weeks to relax and reset so I’m happy to be back with the boys and looking forward to the new season.”

We start in Hong Kong against Italian champions Inter on Saturday 1 August, with kick-off at 12:30 (UK).

After that, we go to Seoul to play a K League All-Stars side on Wednesday 5 August and then Atletico Madrid on Sunday 9 August. Both games begin at 12:00 (UK).

All three will be available to watch on mancity.com and our official app for current CITY+ subscribers globally*.

Available for £34.99 for an annual subscription or £9.99 per month, CITY+ gets you closer to the Club than ever before, with documentaries, live games and full-match replays throughout the season.

*City v Inter: Globally available except China, Italy

K League All-Stars v City: Globally available except South Korea

City v Atletico Madrid: Globally available except South Korea, Spain

title: Usman Nurmagomedov welcomes ‘little short’ guy Archie Colgan to try and wrestle him: ‘He’s not going to win’
description: Usman Nurmagomedov isn’t afraid to grapple with Archie Colgan in their title fight
fullText:
Usman Nurmagomedov has been one of the most dominant fighters in the PFL but much like his coach and cousin Khabib Nurmagomedov, there’s always going to be certain stylistic matchups that makes it look like he’s vulnerable.

Throughout Khabib’s illustrious career, the question always came up ‘what happens if he faces a dominant wrestler?’ The former UFC lightweight champion answered by putting together a perfect 29-0 record before retiring from the sport to focus on coaching.

Now it’s Usman’s turn to provide his own answers as he takes on former college wrestler turned top lightweight contender Archie Colgan in his latest title defense. But don’t expect the reigning PFL lightweight king to show any fear going up against another wrestler in his latest title defense.

“He’s a little short, uncomfortable fighter,” Nurmagomedov said about Colgan when speaking to MMA Fighting. “He’s wrestling very well but I’m from Dagestsan. I can wrestle, I can grapple, I can do Muay Thai. I can do anything.  Whatever he will compete with me, I am going to be better at. All respect for Archie and his team. He’s not going to win.

“I don’t think he’s going to take me down. This is very hard to take me down, to be honest. I know how I have to fight with little short guys. I always love to fight with the little short guys. I have a longer reach. I can control everything.”

While the wrestling question is going to come up often leading into this main event clash, Nurmagomedov is quick to point out that he’s not wrestling Colgan — they are fighting. Nurmagomedov is confident he can match Colgan anywhere on the feet or on the ground and if they want to settle the wrestling debate there’s another way that can happen.

“I think I’m going to grapple with him, too,” Nurmagomedov said. “I think I can take him down. My wrestling is not bad. We can do it like this. I’m going to beat him or knock him down, I know I’m going to beat this guy. For the people if they want to see who is better in the wrestling, we can do it in RAF.”

If anything, Nurmagomedov really hopes that Colgan can bring out the best in him because that’s what he always wants when he’s going out to defend his title.

“I think I have a big potential inside of me,” Nurmagomedov said. “I have very big ambitions. I just need somebody with who I can show this for the people.”

As far as the future goes, Nurmagomedov is undoubtedly going to be bombarded with questions about what comes next as he competes on Friday’s PFL card on the final fight of his contract.

There’s been heavy speculation that Nurmagomedov plans to leave PFL and sign with the UFC, especially now that his teammate and friend Islam Makhachev left the lightweight division to compete at welterweight instead.

Nurmagomedov hasn’t made any decisions yet and he’s doing his absolute best to shut out all the noise until after his fight.

He knows getting distracted is the perfect recipe for disaster if he’s not putting his full focus on Colgan and the fight directly ahead of him.

“Archie, he’s undefeated,” Nurmagomedov said. “You can’t stay like this for a long time [being undefeated] if you’re not in the top five. That’s why he’s the No. 1 contender and of course, he wants to take everything what I have.

“I don’t want to look ahead and thinking about the future for my career. I have a fight. I have a name. We’re going to fight. I have a fight and we have to do this.”

title: Battle of the Hawgs – Preview for the Chicago Bears’ Training Camp Battle at Center
description: Our guy @EDuerrwaechter gives his takes on the Bears’ upcoming battle at Center.
fullText:
As we’ve finally made it to Training Camp for the Chicago Bears, and there shall be a slew of competitions at multiple positions across the roster. Most recently, head coach Ben Johnson confirmed there will be such a contest for the starting job at Center. The two contestants are veteran Garrett Bradbury and rookie Logan Jones.

Regardless of who ultimately wins the job this season, all signs point to Logan Jones becoming *the* guy at Center for 2027 and beyond. That being said, the youngster from Iowa will have his chance to unseat the veteran in Bradbury, who was acquired this offseason via trade from the New England Patriots. I firmly believe this is the most underrated competition to watch at Halas Hall this year.

Previous team(s): NC State Wolfpack; Minnesota Vikings; New England Patriots

The former 18th overall pick of the 2019 NFL Draft has started in all 105 career games he dressed for between the Vikings and the Patriots. Just coming off a Super Bowl run with the Patriots he was also in a similar situation when they selected current starter Jared Wilson with the 95th overall pick and played him at guard during his rookie season. While there was no competition during training camp in Foxborough, he cemented himself as a key cog for an efficient group which spearheaded one of the most dangerous offenses in the league. Nothing spectacular, just solid. And solid is all the Bears need at Center for the time being.

Naturally, the Bears didn’t plan for this transition to happen so soon in the first place. Pro Bowler Drew Dalman was just 27 years old and coming off his best season of his career before abruptly retiring in the spring. This caused Ben Johnson and Ryan Poles to scramble for both an immediate and long-term solution to their center position on relatively short notice. Ultimately, they pivoted towards a trade that landed Garrett Bradbury. He now reunites with a former NC State teammate in All-Pro Guard and reigning Protector of the Year Joe Thuney as well.

What I will point out is that offensive line coach Dan Roushar has only seen one rookie in his career take the mantle as his team’s starting center – Erik McCoy in 2019. Then again, Garrett Bradbury himself started in every game as a rookie too. The center position is by far the most difficult to learn as you have to master both calling protections and your techniques between snapping the ball and identifying the first threat from inside. A team pursuing their own run at the Super Bowl, like the Bears, may not have the appetite for a learning curve at center.

Previous Team(s): Iowa Hawkeyes

Here we have the young challenger to the Bears’ job at Center. While he doesn’t have any experience as a pro just yet, there is a ton of buzz surrounding this latest selection from the OL factory known as Iowa Hawkeye brand football. And it’s not just because the jersey number (54) has returned to the Bears’ lineup.

The Bears picked him as the first center to hear their name called during the 2026 NFL Draft at selection number 57 overall. A spot that has seen great history for the Bears from previous draft classes, including one Devin Hester. The Heinz 57 sponsored product brings with him an excellent set of physical tools anchored by sound technique and a keen awareness for how protections are set. He was named the recipient of the 2025 Rimington Trophy as the nation’s top ranked center in NCAA football as well.

A player most frequently brought up as a pro comparison for Logan Jones – Drew Dalman. Their physicality and athleticism from the center position are reminiscent to each other, where you can see both players pulling naturally when called upon in protection or road paving. The Bears had Logan Jones as their top choice at Center from the start of the process and pounced on him when he was still there in the second round.

There have not been a ton of rookies to start and finish a full season at center for the Bears in recent history. The last such occurrence was in 2016 when Cody Whitehair was kicked inside shortly after the surprise signing of All-Pro Guard Josh Sitton. Even Olin Kruetz himself started just one game during his rookie season. Yet I’d argue the Bears haven’t drafted a pure center who’s nearly as good as Logan Jones is in quite some time.

From the moment his name was called there always was a chance for him to compete for a starting job this year instead of waiting until Garrett Bradbury’s eventual departure. When the pads come on starting next Monday, his opportunities will open up. I’d expect this competition to last all the way until the second preseason game.

Even though Garrett Bradbury is listed as a few pounds heavier, their wingspans are almost identical, with Garrett Bradbury being measured at 1.94m (6ft 4-1/2in) and Logan Jones at 1.93m (6ft 4in). I would almost be willing to bet that Logan Jones will be at or around 305 pounds solid by the end of this season as well.

This is almost self-explanatory, as we have an 8-year veteran with 105 career starts going against a rookie. That experience will come in handy as the Bears look to get into an offensive groove as quickly as possible.

Logan Jones is almost as perfect of a fit for what both Ben Johnson and Dan Roushar want at center that you can possibly imagine. While Bradbury is no slouch himself with a 4.92 forty compared to Jones’ 4.90 forty, Jones wins hands-down in the 3-cone time with a stunning 7.35, in comparison to a respectable 7.41 by Bradbury. What’s more is Jones’ athleticism pops on film as he can run any protection asked of him, while Bradbury has occasionally struggled when tasked to pull or slide in protection. Jones is extremely powerful at the point of attack as well.

What I’m looking at here is seeing who can be counted on right this second to line up and play center for the Bears if a game were happening at the time this article was published. Garrett Bradbury has all the experience, technical expertise, and knowledge of protections to identify the first threat before the ball is snapped. His previous chemistry with Joe Thuney is a plus as well. It is a very tall task for any rookie to line up at center during week one.

Much like the experience question above, this is blatantly obvious. Never mind the 7-year age difference between each player, their contracts also are drastically different. Garrett Bradbury signed a revised deal following his arrival to Chicago which amounts to 1-year and $4.7M. Out of the total value $3.7M is fully guaranteed with an additional $1M moved to what’s called Not Likely to be Earned (NLTBE) incentives. Logan Jones is on the standard 4-year rookie contract with a pre-slotted $8.47M and a $2.12M annual average.

Yes, I did literally just say I’d expect Garrett Bradbury to get the nod if a game happened while I’m sitting at my desk typing this article. However, if Logan Jones performs well enough during training camp, then I cannot see Ben Johnson turning down a chance for the future to begin right away at center. I’m not simply saying he needs to be adequate – he needs to be outstanding for him to unseat Garrett Bradbury. I.E. dominate from the very moment the pads come on. Otherwise, the job will go to Garrett Bradbury, and Logan Jones will wait his turn. Whether that is in 2027 or this season is up to a multitude of factors.

Who do you think opens week one with the starters at center?

title: SSFC Spotlight: Colton Swan tearing up the second division
description: The forward is lighting up the USL Championship.
fullText:
The United States Under-20 Men’s National Team is currently competing at the 2026 CONCACAF U-20 Championship, seeking to qualify for the 2027 U-20 World Cup and the 2027 Pan American Games by reaching the semifinal round. Additionally, the tournament provides a glimpse at some of the up-and-coming talent for the respective sides, which could inspire some optimism for the future of the program. Colton Swan is one of the more experienced names on the roster, having entered the professional ranks after several seasons in the reserves and college. The 19-year-old Charleston Battery forward is nearing double figures in his first USL Championship campaign and could be set for a big transfer.

Raised in Detroit, Michigan, Swan competed with Michigan Tigers and Michigan Jaguars, winning three state cups and a United States Youth Soccer National Championship while being named to the National League and National Championship Best XI after compiling 30 goals and 12 assists. Following trials with the Seattle Sounders and Nashville SC, he then joined the Colorado Rapids academy, picking up 34 goals and 14 assists and receiving the U-16 MLS Cup Golden Boot and Best XI honors. The forward began featuring with the reserves in MLS NEXT Pro, contributing two goals and one assist in 15 matches in 2024, followed by four goals and two assists in 13 fixtures in 2025, earning multiple Rising Star of the Week and Month citations.

“The steps for me have been very quick,” Swan told USL All Access. “In transition from playing with Michigan Tigers, moving up to Michigan Jags, moving up another level with Colorado, then breaking into the second team, getting some first team reps. Obviously, I would have loved to have signed there, a first-team deal, but things did not go the way I wanted to. I don’t think they rated me very high as a player … I was planning on playing with the Rapids, and I didn’t have much hope of signing a contract, in my opinion … There was a second-team contract on the table, but for me, at that point, my family [and I] decided that it’d be a better route to go to college and from there figure it out.”

Rated a four-star recruit by TopDrawerSoccer, Swan then matriculated at Indiana University, described as “one of the premier front-runners in the country” and a “lethal finisher inside the box and especially in the air.” In his sole collegiate campaign, he started in 11 out of his 19 appearances and added three goals and three assists as the Hoosiers fell in the second round of the NCAA Tournament. The Big Ten named him Freshman of the Week for the final week of the season and to the Big Ten All-Freshman Team.

In January of 2026, Swan joined the professional ranks and signed “a multi-year contract” with the Charleston Battery in the USL Championship. A “unique prospect with a tremendous ability to improve,” he quickly entered into the rotation and then the starting lineup, racking up nine goals and three assists in 18 matches across all competitions. The league named him the Player of the Month for May, the youngest winner in competition history, being praised for his “great mentality: hungry, tenacious, genuinely selfless for [his] club, and wanting to improve.” According to Tom Bogert of The Athletic, “a handful of MLS sides reached out” to kick the tires on a potential transfer.

At the international level, Swan began playing with the United States in the Under-18 age group, helping to win the 2025 UEFA Friendship Cup with a goal in the opener against France. He was also included on the Under-19 roster for June’s training camp that concluded with a 5-2 rout of Japan. Manager Gonzalo Segares named him to the roster for the 2026 CONCACAF U-20 Championship – which will determine qualification for the 2027 FIFA U-20 World Cup and 2027 Pan American Games – utilizing him for the final seven minutes in the opening 3-0 victory over Haiti and in the second half of the 3-0 win against El Salvador.

Standing at six feet, two inches tall, Swan is a striker who gets several shots on target and serves as a reliable creator, due to “physical traits that are beyond most, [the drive to attack] the box, and always looking to link up with teammates.” He works “every day in and out” on being aggressive and believes that being lethal in the six “has to be [his] superpower,” believing that headed finishes are “a lost skill” in the modern game. Observers describe him as having “speed and a good first step” with an ability to “play back to goal.”

“My head [is working], per usual,” Swan said after a recent match. “It’s something that [is] definitely a huge part of my game, especially being a number nine, in my profile as a player. That’s something that’s been a super strength for me since I was 10 years old … When the ball’s flying my way, I just try to do my best to put it in the net. But, yeah, [I am] a bit pass-first. I would say that’s been my game my entire life … Most forwards, they’re taught to pass more later, people get on them for dribbling or shooting too much … I just love moving the rock. I love passing the ball, but scoring the ball is just that much more fun, honestly.”

Swan has picked up valuable experience in a variety of set-ups, journeying from the MLS reserves to college and now the USL Championship and the youth international ranks. While he has proven to be a reliable finisher, time will tell if his production will continue or diminish when given a chance at successively higher levels of play. If the forward is able to make the squad and contribute at the U-20 World Cup, then elevation and the opportunity to insert himself into the senior conversation will follow swiftly.

title: U.S. wins two team medals at World Fencing Championships
description: The U.S. made the podium in women's and men's team foil, traditionally its most successful of the three fencing disciplines.
fullText:
The U.S. finished the World Fencing Championships with two medals — silver in women's team foil and bronze in men's team foil, continuing its strong recent tradition in the foil discipline.

In women's team foil, Italy defeated the U.S. 45-29 in Thursday's final in Hong Kong in a rematch of the 2024 Olympic gold-medal match.

Lauren Scruggs was the lone holdover from the Olympic champion team. She was joined by Jaelyn Liu and Carolina Stutchbury in the final, plus Josephina Conway, who competed in the opening round.

Scruggs, the 2024 Olympic silver medalist in the individual foil, and Liu were also on the team that won the 2025 World title.

Lee Kiefer, who won the last two individual Olympic foil gold medals, was in Hong Kong but did not compete as she is pregnant with her first child.

The U.S. men's foil team of Nick Itkin, Alexander Massialas, Bryce Louie and Marcello Olivares earned bronze on Tuesday.

They were edged in the semifinals by host Hong Kong 45-43, then crushed Japan 45-28 in the bronze-medal match.

Over the last decade, the U.S. won a medal in men's team foil at two of the three Olympics (bronze at Rio 2016, Tokyo 2020) and six of the seven World Championships.

In individual events at these worlds, three Americans reached the quarterfinals -- Scruggs in women's foil, fellow 2024 Olympian Hadley Husisian in women's epee and Darii Lukashenko in men's sabre.

title: Indiana football's Nick Marsh more than flashy footwear
description: Nick Marsh's former teammates weren't surprised he wore gold cleats. They also won't be shocked when he turns into Indiana football's top playmaker:
fullText:
CHICAGO — Michigan State linebacker Jordan Hall had a smile on his face at Big Ten Media Days on Wednesday talking about his former teammate Nick Marsh’s unique dress sense.

After the 2025 season, Indiana football signed the talented receiver out of the transfer portal. Marsh made a splashy entrance on the first day of spring camp by busting out a pair of gold cleats in violation of Curt Cignetti’s strict uniform policy.

Cignetti sent Marsh right back to the locker room.

“It didn't surprise me that he yelled at him,” Hall said with a laugh. “It didn't surprise me that he was wearing it.”

More: Indiana football commands respect at Big Ten Media Days

Hall knew all about Cignetti’s exacting standards from former IU linebacker Aiden Fisher — they kept in touch as childhood friends from Fredericksburg, Virginia — and Marsh’s bold fashion choices.

“Last year (at Big Ten Media Days) he wore an orange suit,” Hall said.

Marsh sported a matching bow tie to complete the ensemble.

“He loves his style,” Michigan State quarterback Alessio Milivojevic said. “It fit him very well.”

While MSU players appreciated Marsh’s fashion sense, they were more impressed with his skill set, one they believe will set him up for success in Bloomington. Marsh spent two seasons with the Spartans, and led the team in receiving in both of them.

In 2025, Marsh also ranked first on the squad in receptions (59, 10th-most in the Big Ten) and receiving touchdowns (six). He ranked third among receivers in the FBS with 28 forced missed tackles in just 12 games, one more than Omar Cooper Jr. for the Hoosiers in 16 games.

“On the field, he can go and do it all pretty much,” Milivojevic said of Marsh. “He can go up and get it. He's a big bodied guy. He's a great route runner.”

More: Ohio State knows atmosphere has changed at Indiana football this year

Michigan State safety Nikai Martinez quickly recognized Marsh’s talent as well. The multi-year starter identified Marsh as a player to watch the minute the receiver stepped on campus.

“I always knew he was one of those ones as a receiver, and just how good and how much he knew being a freshman,” Martinez said. “And the talent level he had, and just the plays that we could see that he made, I always knew he had that spark in him.”

Like Milivojevic, Martinez raved about Marsh’s abilities.

“His hands, he has very strong hands,” Martinez said. “And just being able to locate the ball, and just a big body, and the way he moves. For a person that big, he can move, and he's agile, and he just can make people miss.”

Those talents will help Marsh make headlines this season beyond his footwear choice.

“Nick’s a great kid,” Hall said. “I'm sure Coach Cignetti and that staff will appreciate his assets that he can bring.”

Michael Niziolek is the Indiana beat reporter for The Bloomington Herald-Times. You can follow him on X @michaelniziolek and read all his coverage by clicking here.

title: Auburn hitter earns SEC preseason nod after strong sophomore season
description: Auburn volleyball will rely heavily on hitter Lauren Dreves as they look to capitalize on their 17-win campaign last season.
fullText:
Expectations surrounding hitter Lauren Dreves have risen entering the 2026 season after she made a splash as a sophomore for Auburn volleyball last season.

Dreves, who landed an All-SEC honor last season as well as a spot on the AVCA First Team All-South Region team, has been named to the Preseason All-SEC team ahead of the 2026 season. She lands a spot on the team alongside fellow outside hitters Jordyn Byrd (Florida), Bianna Muoneke (Georgia), and Jurnee Robinson (LSU).

Dreves made a name for herself last season by logging 375 kills and 16 assists offensively while recording 220 digs and 64 blocks on defense. Dreves set three season highs in Auburn's road match at LSU by recording 24 kills, 24.5 points, and 15 digs in Baton Rouge. She also made six blocks against Kentucky last October and three assists against Texas last November.

Auburn volleyball will look to Dreves to lead the program as they look to capitalize on their 17-win campaign in 2025. Auburn was picked to finish seventh in the SEC this season with 142 points, one spot behind Georgia and ahead of LSU. Kentucky is projected to win the SEC this season with nine first-place votes. Texas is next in line with 216 points and six first-place votes.

title: Chiefs DB Alohi Gilman discusses his role as a leader in the secondary
description: During his press conference, Kansas City Chiefs safety Alohi Gilman discussed his role as a veteran leader in the secondary | @EdEastonJr
fullText:
Kansas City Chiefs defensive back Alohi Gilman spoke with reporters after practice on Wednesday at Missouri Western State University. He discussed the young players in the secondary and his role as a veteran leader in the unit.

"I mean, just this group is a a little bit more quiet than I said than other DB personalities that I've been around. So it's been a little bit harder to get the shell out of them a little more. So I would take them out to dinner every week during OTAs. Take them out, we'll hang out, just little stuff like that, and they're a great group," said Gilman. "I love every single one of them." They've welcomed me with open arms and are just hard workers, just straight to the point, kind of like me, kind of a no-nonsense, just get to work and let's get after it kind of people."

The veteran safety has recorded 320 tackles, 1 sack, 5 interceptions, and 6 fumble recoveries in his six-year career. He appreciates the role of a veteran leader on the team among young players in his unit, without having to be the most vocal.

"I've evolved in that as well as a player. I wouldn't say I'm the loudest, but you know I feel like when I speak, my words mean a lot," said Gilman. "I try to be as genuine as possible, and be a friend, be a brother, and that's kind of how I approach it."

Gilman signed a three-year, $24.75 million deal with $15 million guaranteed. In 2025, he started all 17 games for the Los Angeles Chargers and the Baltimore Ravens, recording 90 tackles.

title: ESPN hypes SEC strength of schedule in latest myth-making exercise
description: The SEC is no longer the dominant conference in college football. Not only has the Big Ten won the last three national championships, but the SEC has also been soundly beaten in postseason games. But that’s not stopping the league from puffing out its chest once again. And it just so happens that their billion-dollar…
fullText:
The SEC is no longer the dominant conference in college football. Not only has the Big Ten won the last three national championships, but the SEC has also been soundly beaten in postseason games. But that’s not stopping the league from puffing out its chest once again.

And it just so happens that their billion-dollar rights partners at ESPN are helping push the narrative yet again.

It’s a cycle that seems to recur every year and makes college football fans feel as if they’re living their own version of Bill Murray’s Groundhog Day.

It’s a cycle that repeats itself continuously. SEC teams often have artificially inflated preseason rankings. Teams that have good early starts are rewarded with astronomical gains. The teams that lose aren’t punished because of the perceived strength of the opposition. Even though the SEC has been called out, the conference’s adherents (including plenty of voices on ESPN) treat it as definitive proof of superiority, even though it’s based more on conjecture and hypothetical wins than on what happens in reality.

And now the cycle is beginning all over again.

On Tuesday, the ESPN Insights page on X posted a list of teams ranked by the top strength of schedule coming into the 2026 college football season. The post touted the SEC expanding to a nine-game conference schedule and that, according to their metrics, every SEC team made the Top 20 of the rankings. Four Big Ten teams made the cut and none from any other conference.

This season, the SEC will start a 9-game conference schedule

A likely result of the additional conference game is that every SEC team has a strength of schedule in the Top-20, according to ESPN Analytics. pic.twitter.com/F5o3b9qomt

— ESPN Insights (@ESPNInsights) July 28, 2026

Immediately, social media was filled with comments and complaints that not only accused the network of stumping once again for their rights partner, but also the idea of devising strength-of-schedule metrics before a game has even been played.

“Because they play a bunch of SEC teams.”

“Really good, because they play a bunch of SEC teams.”

“How do you know if SEC teams are better than teams from other conferences?”

“They are better, because… https://t.co/cVUDLJ2Exo

— CougarStats (@CougarStats) July 28, 2026

ESPN owns the SEC Network.
 ESPN owns the Playoff broadcast.
 ESPN also builds the strength-of-schedule model that decides which SEC teams belong in the Playoff.
 That’s not a ranking. That’s manipulation. https://t.co/4aXU1Rrbnv

— Miles Shoaf || MSR (@milesashoaf) July 28, 2026

Rhett Lashlee at ACC media days last week:

“Whenever some of y’all figure out how we can have preseason strength of schedules and power rankings before anybody has played a game, y’all let me know.” https://t.co/ZfF3Uw1SQ2

— Steve Helwick (@s_helwick) July 28, 2026

You see, the SEC is tough because they play the SEC who plays the SEC which is tough because they play the SEC who is tough because they play the SEC who plays the SEC https://t.co/52ZI5NmV1E

— Shaloobys (@shaloobys) July 29, 2026

We’ve finally fully realized the SEC Strength of Schedule feedback loop https://t.co/qV0w4KShsX

— CF After Dark (@AfterDarkCF) July 28, 2026

ESPN wants you to believe that a conference that went 1-8 in the postseason vs P4 opponents, is much tougher now that they have the same amount of conf games as everyone else. https://t.co/HgSS88N1YI

— B1Gadier General Daniel A. Lanning (@DuckDMB) July 29, 2026

Allegations that ESPN improperly favors the SEC will always follow the company as long as subjective factors like this influence who has an opportunity to play for a national championship. We are supposed to believe that Ole Miss has one of the Top 5 hardest schedules in the country when they play teams like Auburn, Mississippi State, Missouri, and Florida? When their non-conference lineup features Wofford and Charlotte? Where they miss out on Alabama, Tennessee, and Texas A&M? While it may work with whatever analytics ESPN has produced, it doesn’t pass the common sense test.

The sensible thing to do would be to abolish preseason rankings and only start the process when the College Football Playoff committee releases its own rankings. Give us time to see who is actually good and who is not, and use what happens on the field to evaluate teams instead of projections and opinions. But expecting anything sensible to happen in the college football world means it’s not likely to occur anytime soon.

The post ESPN hypes SEC strength of schedule in latest myth-making exercise appeared first on Awful Announcing.

title: Birmingham sign Palermo left-back Lund
description: Birmingham City sign USA left-back Kristoffer Lund on a four-year contract for an undisclosed fee.
fullText:
Birmingham City have added a fifth new signing in preparation for the new season after agreeing a deal for Palermo defender Kristoffer Lund.

The 24-year-old USA left-back has arrived on a four-year contract for an undisclosed fee.

Denmark-born Lund made his senior debut for FC Midtjylland in 2021, having come through the club's academy, before going on to have a spell in Sweden.

He joined Palermo three years ago and went on to make 72 appearances for the Serie B club before spending last season on loan in Germany with Bundesliga side FC Cologne.

Lund, who has won seven caps for the USA but was not part of their World Cup squad, joins Argentine striker Luis Vazquez, defender Dael Fry, loanee goalkeeper James Beadle and now-permanent signing Jhon Solis at St Andrew's in boss Chris Davies' squad for 2026-27.

title: Should the Seahawks bring Jadeveon Clowney back?
description: Should the Seattle Seahawks bring veteran pass rusher Jadeveon Clowney back?
fullText:
Seattle Seahawks general manager John Schneider believes in keeping the cupboard stocked at defensive end. That's precisely why they made veteran EDGE Dante Fowler Jr. a late-wave free agency signing. Well, another experienced pass rusher with ties to the organization is available.

Veteran EDGE Jadeveon Clowney recently visited the Cleveland Browns, according to NFL Network reporter Mike Garafolo. Aaron Wilson then reported that the Seahawks and Houston Texans also have interest in the experienced quarterback hunter. Should the Seahawks bring Clowney back in 2026?

Possible reunion: DE Jadeveon Clowney is visiting the #Browns today, source says.

Following an 8.5-sack season with the #Cowboys, Clowney is exploring another stint in Cleveland, where he had 11 sacks in two seasons from 2021-22. pic.twitter.com/ikdNM2Ytve

— Mike Garafolo (@MikeGarafolo) July 29, 2026

Clowney played for the Seahawks during the 2019 NFL season. He appeared in 13 contests, registering 31 tackles and three sacks. Clowney has since played for various franchises on one-year contracts. He was with the Dallas Cowboys in 2025, proving he has plenty left in the tank by notching 8.5 sacks in just 13 appearances.

The Seahawks are deep at EDGE. Derick Hall recently signed a lucrative contract extension with the organization. DeMarcus Lawrence and Fowler are expected to play starring roles. Uchenna Nwosu is also an impactful player for Mike Macdonald's defense.

Coach Macdonald loves rotating pass rushers. The Seahawks have EDGEs in numbers, but there's room for Clowney on the roster. Clowney could find a new team soon, and the Seahawks are reportedly interested.

fullText:
The Seattle Storm apologized Wednesday for an interaction involving a team co-owner during Tuesday’s game against the Indiana Fever. The team did not specify what the exchange was, but podcast host Brandi Kruse shared a video Tuesday night of two teenage girls wearing shirts depicting XX and XY chromosomes saying Storm minority owner Celeste Keaton approached them, cursed and called them insane.

The game between the Storm and Fever was Indiana’s first since guard Sophie Cunningham said in an ESPN article that it’s “common sense” to bar transgender athletes from competing in women’s sports.

Kruse also shared a photo of the girls holding up a sign courtside that read, “Thank you Sophie for speaking up for girls.” Before the game, a small group of fans gathered outside Seattle’s Climate Pledge Arena holding signs in support of Cunningham, according to The Associated Press.

“Everyone who attends a Storm game deserves to feel welcome, and we remain committed to creating an inclusive environment where every fan is treated with respect,” Storm majority owner Ginny Gilder said in the team’s apology.

In addition to the apology, the WNBA suspended Keaton from attending the Storm’s next five home games and fined the team an undisclosed amount, the league confirmed Thursday.

In response to a post about the apology, Cunningham wrote on X late Wednesday: “Truly embarrassing of the co-owner. Unfortunately shows the type of leader she is.”

She added: “I truly believe there is a safe space and love for EVERYBODY. Biological girls, biological boys, trans women, and trans men. Everyone is welcome at my table! You can disagree and still be kind.”

The social media post was Cunningham’s first comment since the publication of the ESPN article. After Indiana won Tuesday’s game, the team did not make Cunningham or star guard Caitlin Clark available to speak with reporters.

“Neither our organization nor Sophie had any knowledge of this demonstration and no contact with its organizers,” the Indiana Fever said in a statement. “Our only goal as a team, whether at home or away, is to win basketball games and make Fever fans for life, and we are united in that mission.”

Devon Henderson contributed to this report.

title: 'Hamilton comes in only when all the photographers are there, so he can wear the ridiculous clothing'
description: Former Formula 1 team principal Otmar Szafnauer has drawn a contrast between Lewis Hamilton and Max Verstappen, praising the Red Bull driver's work ethic while making a pointed comparison with the Ferrari star. Speaking on the High Performance Podcast, Szafnauer posed a rhetorical question about which Formula 1 driver is always the first to arrive at the circuit.
fullText:
Former Formula 1 team principal Otmar Szafnauer has drawn a contrast between Lewis Hamilton and Max Verstappen, praising the Red Bull driver's work ethic while making a pointed comparison with the Ferrari star.

Speaking on the High Performance Podcast, Szafnauer posed a rhetorical question about which Formula 1 driver is always the first to arrive at the circuit. When host Jake Humphrey suggested Max Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton, the former team principal interrupted to make it clear there was only one correct answer: Verstappen.

"Max Verstappen. He is always the first in,” Szafnauer said firmly. He then explained that Hamilton has a very different habit when he arrives at the circuit. According to the Romanian-American, the seven-time world champion actually chooses to get to the track later, so the photographers on site can capture his eye-catching outfits. "Lewis comes in only when all the photographers are there, so he can wear the ridiculous clothing and take pictures."
 That remark sparks a light-hearted discussion at the table. Humphrey stood up for the Ferrari driver and says he’s actually a fan of Hamilton’s fashion style. Szafnauer, in turn, can’t relate to that at all. "Really? What is it?" he responded, after which the host explained that Hamilton, in his view, mainly dares to stand out - something Szafnauer did acknowledge.

"He can pull it off, I can’t," the former team principal added. He then gave a playful nod to Hamilton’s private life: "I think the fashion helped with Kim Kardashian, without a doubt."

title: UNC opens fall camp as questions linger over GM Michael Lombardi's leave
description: The start of camp also comes as UNC navigates an off-field issue involving general manager Michael Lombardi, who was recently placed on administrative leave.
fullText:
North Carolina football opens fall camp Thursday as the Tar Heels begin preparations for the 2026 season under head coach Bill Belichick.

The start of camp also comes as UNC navigates an off-field issue involving general manager Michael Lombardi, who was recently placed on administrative leave. UNC announced the decision Monday and has not publicly released additional details about it.

Ahead of Thursday's media availability, UNC released a statement saying it is investigating the circumstances that led to Lombardi's leave.

"As a result of concerns behind allegations that led to the personnel action regarding Michael Lombardi announced on July 27, the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill, through its Office of University Counsel, is in the process of investigating this matter. Because this involves confidential personnel issues, the University will not comment on the nature of the allegations or discuss personnel information."

A university spokesperson also said before the news conference that coaches, staff and student-athletes are prohibited from discussing the matter.

Coach Belichick spoke to reporters around 8:30 a.m.

Earlier this week, ABC11 spoke with ESPN's David Hale, who said colleague Pete Thamel reported the issue "revolves around an HR dispute for someone who was let go by Michael Lombardi, where there's an internal investigation that's ongoing, and that's where the suspension comes from."

Lombardi joined Belichick at UNC in December 2024, reuniting with the six-time Super Bowl-winning coach. He worked under Belichick with the New England Patriots from 2014 to 2016 and earlier with the Cleveland Browns beginning in 1987.

Lombardi has faced scrutiny on multiple occasions during his time in Chapel Hill, including when he said in February 2025 that the Tar Heels "consider ourselves the 33rd NFL team." He also made headlines last September when he informed the Patriots that their scouts would be banned from access to the Tar Heels' program.

UNC went 4-8 last season under Belichick and did not have any players selected in this year's NFL draft.

The Tar Heels open their second season under Belichick on Aug. 29 against TCU in Dublin, Ireland.

Separately, the UNC Board of Trustees was scheduled to meet at 9:30 a.m. Thursday.

ESPN contributed to this report.

title: Reports: Leverkusen talent Alajbegovic to June for €30 million
description: Bayer Leverkusen talent Kerim Alajbegovic is reportedly close to joining Italy's Juventus. German media including Kicker sports magazine and the Bild paper said on Thursday that Leverkusen will receive €30 million ($34.
fullText:
Bayer Leverkusen talent Kerim Alajbegovic is reportedly close to joining Italy's Juventus.

German media including Kicker sports magazine and the Bild paper said on Thursday that Leverkusen will receive €30 million ($34.2 million) plus add-ons for the 18-year-old from the Turin club.

Alajbegovic, who played at the recent World Cup for Bosnia-Herzegovina, is to sign a five-year contract at Juve who according to the reports have promised him a role in the starting XI, something that Leverkusen apparently would not guarantee.

Alajbegovic started in the academy of Bundesliga club Cologne in his city of birth before moving to neighbours Leverkusen in 2021. Leverkusen sold him to RB Salzburg last year but made use of a buy-back clause of €8 million.

title: Inter in Hong Kong: club legends come together ahead of the clash with Manchester City
description: HONG KONG – Inter have arrived in Hong Kong for the Internazionale Summer Tour, with the Nerazzurri’s Asian adventure getting underway among media activities and events.Christian Vieri and Shaun W...
fullText:
HONG KONG – Inter have arrived in Hong Kong for the Internazionale Summer Tour, with the Nerazzurri’s Asian adventure getting underway among media activities and events.

Christian Vieri and Shaun Wright-Phillips, legends of FC Internazionale Milano and Manchester City respectively, met ahead of the two teams’ summer friendly, joining past and present in an international setting.

It was a symbolic event, featuring photos with the city skyline in the background and content creation sessions.

The pair also took part in an exclusive interview, discussing the importance of pre-season training and facing top-level opponents early in the campaign.

“Pre-season is the most important period,” explained Vieri, “because that’s when you build the foundations. The season will stretch on; you play every three days: the more work you do now, the better.”

Wright-Phillips also shared this view: "It's fundamental, it's like putting money in the bank. You build a foundation, and from there you can only improve."

Both then highlighted the importance of the clash between Inter and Manchester City.

“When you face a top team in front of thousands of fans, nobody wants to lose,” added Vieri.

“There’s no better test,” echoed Wright-Phillips. “You always want to measure yourself against the best, and that’s what this match will do.”

Inter’s activities in Asia will continue in the coming days, with the Nerazzurri preparing for their first fixture of the tour.

title: Mercedes impressed by "sizeable" McLaren upgrade after Hungarian GP defeat
description: Mercedes deputy technical director Simone Resta opens up on the increased competition the championship-leading squad has faced in recent weeks
fullText:
Mercedes was impressed by Lando Norris' victory aboard the upgraded McLaren at last weekend's Hungarian Grand Prix, while detailing its own efforts to improve both reliability and performance.

Norris ended Mercedes' perfect pole record during 2026 in Budapest before going on to dominate Sunday's race for the Woking outfit’s first grand prix win of the season.

It came after McLaren fitted a redesigned floor onto the Mercedes-powered MCL40, which Mercedes discussed on its new in-house podcast, the Nu Silver Arrows Radio Show.

Mercedes’ deputy technical director Simone Resta said: "For sure, it's a sizeable update and it must have had an impact on their performance.

"But also, if you look at the gap between their two cars, it's significant as well. We have seen, in general, McLaren as a team that has performed well on many occasions this year with a bit of up and down between the two drivers in terms of who is the fastest one.

"We have seen some strong performances from Norris already every time this year. And maybe he was in a very good place with the car and the set-up in these conditions and tyre management and he executed very well. So I think it's probably a combination of both aspects."

The current season started with Mercedes domination, winning the opening six grands prix from pole, but Ferrari and McLaren have both since won races thanks to upgrades.

Now after recouping 26 points over the last three weekends, Ferrari trails championship leader Mercedes by 72 points heading into the summer break.

Despite the radically new chassis and power unit regulations providing plenty of scope for the grid to be stretched out, Resta said Mercedes had expected the competition to be as close as it has become in recent months.

"Yes, we were broadly expecting that," the former Ferrari man said. "Clearly, you only start the season with question marks about potential other contenders, but actually it panned out as we expected.

“It's great to see these teams developing perhaps on a very slightly different development scenario with different upgrades at different times. It's nice to see some fluctuation of performance, which I guess is making the racing quite more interesting."

One factor in the competition making inroads is Mercedes' on-going power unit problems and other reliability gremlins, which has cost it numerous points over the first half of the season.

Resta vowed the team is tackling its issues with "relentless effort".

"I think this is as a result of the level being higher in Formula 1," the Italian added. "You really need to squeeze out everything in every single aspect, and we are lucky we got a lot of experience in the team.

“We've got good processes, good tools. We just have to really keep our relentless effort in just nailing them one by one with the right prioritisation.

"Nothing emotional, just simply rationally analyse all of them, make sure we have the right fix at the right time and speed up this process. We'll be a better team after we sort out all of this."

Meanwhile, Mercedes is weighing up its own upgrade programme over the second half of 2026 after seeing its rivals bringing much bigger packages so far.

"Those are the conversations that are happening at the minute," said deputy team principal Bradley Lord. "When do we bring the performance that's in the wind tunnel or working its way through the factory at the moment?

"What races do we introduce those, where do things come with the ADUO opportunity on the power unit, with the aero upgrades on the chassis as well? And making sure we're pacing that in the right way and not tripping ourselves up by trying to almost overreach too quickly."

title: Phillies reportedly have had trade talks with Angels over .757 OPS shortstop
description: This Phillies trade target would be a very fascinating, but expensive one.
fullText:
Phillies reportedly have had trade talks with Angels over .757 OPS shortstop originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

The Philadelphia Phillies are in a bit of a free-fall since the All-Star break. Things are not going well at all, and this team desperately needs help at the trade deadline.

While the starting rotation and bullpen need help in a bad way, the real need is with the lineup. It's been a rough offensive showing this season, and they desperately need better firepower, especially from the right side of the plate.

ESPN's Jeff Passan reported on SportsCenter that the Phillies are showing serious interest in Los Angeles Angels right-handed hitting shortstop Zach Neto, already having trade talks about the young infielder in what could be a very fascinating acquisition.

"They've had conversations with the Los Angeles Angels about Zach Neto, who, you say, Trea Turner is a shortstop already, Trea Turner might not be at shortstop long-term, and having a guy of Zach Neto's caliber not just with his glove, but especially with the bat, with the power, would really help that lineup," Passan said.

What will the Phillies do ahead of the trade deadline?@JeffPassan shares potential routes that could make an impact in Philadelphia 👀 pic.twitter.com/7Pw93zy5Cw

— SportsCenter (@SportsCenter) July 30, 2026

Neto is a 25-year-old shortstop from the Angels who is under club control through the 2029 season. He'd be the Phillies new shortstop for the next 3.5 seasons if they could pull off such a deal.

But if they add Neto, the Phillies will need to move Trea Turner from his spot at shortstop, which, all things considered, would probably be a good thing. He's struggled there defensively this season, and moving him to the outfield or second base would work.

MORE: Red Sox ‘would love’ to trade for Angels’ Zach Neto or Astros’ Jeremy Pena

Adding Neto, who has a .757 OPS this season with 21 doubles, 19 home runs, 97 hits, and 2.8 bWAR (which would be the most of any Phillies position player this season), would be a significant trade for the Phillies.

Dave Dombrowski would have to part with some very talented prospects, likely sending Gage Wood and/or Ramon Marquez to get such a deal across the finish line. Francisco Renteria or Aidan Miller might even have to be included as well.

A trade for Neto will cost a fortune, and the fit on the roster is very fascinating. But there's no denying that he would be an upgrade both offensively and defensively for the Phillies.

This is one potential trade that Phillies fans should keep their eyes on, as Neto to Philadelphia seems to be a fairly realistic possibility, even at the steep price tag for such a deal.

title: Wrexham eager to chart a pathway to the Premier League next season
description: Wrexham will head into the 2026/27 Championship season as one of the favourites to win promotion to the Premier League.Some impressive pre-season performances have raised expectations around a club wh...
fullText:
Wrexham will head into the 2026/27 Championship season as one of the favourites to win promotion to the Premier League.

Some impressive pre-season performances have raised expectations around a club which has enjoyed a meteoric rise in recent years.

After drawing with Wisla Krakow (0-0), the Welsh club recorded victories over Manchester United (1-0) and Leeds United (3-2).

A narrow 1-0 defeat against Liverpool at Yankee Stadium in New York failed to dampen enthusiasm around the club.

Wrexham have undoubtedly come a long way since co-owners Ryan Reynolds and Rob McElhenney completed their purchase of the club in 2021.

Their investment has helped the Dragons climb from the National League to the Championship. They are just one promotion away from the top flight.

Manager Phil Parkinson is now eager to complete the journey. He believes their pre-season results highlight the progress they have made.

“You play Man United, Leeds and Liverpool and you come away with a single-goal defeat as your worst result out of the three, you have to say that’s not a bad result,” he said.

“In terms of the performance, we’re learning as a team. When we’re under a little bit of pressure and we get the ball back, that’s when we have to lift the game and give ourselves a breather with the ball.

“When we did that, I thought we did okay.”

Wrexham kicked off their summer transfer business with the signing of wing-back Danny Imray from Crystal Palace for an undisclosed fee.

The 23-year-old spent the second half of last season on loan at West Bromwich Albion and produced a series of impressive performances.

More new signings are expected at Wrexham, with the co-owners willing to sanction another major spending spree this summer.

Sunderland goalkeeper Anthony Patterson and Everton shot-stopper Mark Travers are potential transfer targets.

Leicester City defender Harry Souttar has also been linked with the club, although the £10m asking price is a stumbling block.

Senegal forward Bamba Dieng has been touted as a possible option, but a move for Portsmouth defender Terry Devlin is unlikely following the Imray deal.

More potential targets will emerge during August as Wrexham strive to win promotion to the Premier League at the second time of asking.

Wrexham agonisingly missed out on the play-offs last term as they finished two points behind Hull City, who subsequently went on to win the play-off final.

The English Football League’s decision to expand the Championship play-offs from four teams to six should work to Wrexham’s advantage.

West Ham United and Wolverhampton Wanderers are expected to be in contention for automatic promotion following their relegation from the top flight.

Burnley, Middlesbrough and Birmingham City are other clubs who will expect to be challenging for a top two spot.

Wrexham’s investment in their squad could bring them into the equation, although a place in the expanded play-offs is a more likely target.

Sheffield United, Norwich City and Derby County are amongst a plethora of clubs who will be eyeing a top eight finish.

If Wrexham can spend their transfer kitty wisely, there is no reason why they can’t mount a sustained challenge for promotion.

However, given the strength of the Championship this season, it would be foolish to think the outcome is a foregone conclusion.

title: Scotland & England face losing Para-race medals
description: Melanie Woods faces losing her Commonwealth Games women’s 1500m T54 title after it is decide to stage the race again following an appeal.
fullText:
Scottish Para-athlete Melanie Woods faces losing her Commonwealth Games women’s 1500m T54 gold - and England's Ellis Kottas her silver - after it was decided to stage the race again following an appeal.

Woods, 31, set a new Games record in streaking to victory in her home city on Wednesday, but the event at Scotstoun was marred by a first-lap crash.

Canada’s Nandini Sharma crossed the line in second place behind Woods, but was disqualified at the time for her role in the incident and Kottas upgraded.

The Canadians‘ appeal against that failed and, after further protests by Australia and Mauritius, the Para-athletics authorities - rather than Glasgow 2026 organisers - have ruled that the event should be restaged on Friday.

Woods took gold ahead of Kottas and Mikaela Dingley of Australia, but the ceremony was not due to be held until Thursday, so none of the athletes were actually presented with medals.

"We note the decision of the jury of appeal regarding the Women's T54 1500m final," Team Scotland said in a statement. "Melanie Woods and Joanna Robertson will now prepare to compete again on Friday in the rerun."

Team England, meanwhile, say they are "incredibly disappointed" with the decision.

"While there is no formal protest process available to us, we have strongly challenged the decision," Jonny Riall, England's chef de mission said.

"The race officials did not halt the race at the time of the incident, nor was any immediate decision made to declare the race void or order a rerun.

"Ellis and the team therefore proceeded on the understanding that all competition procedures had been completed and the result confirmed."

Woods - who has used a wheelchair since being hit by a car while riding her bike in 2018 - is also due to compete in the 400m in Friday's morning session.

The heats of that will start a little more than 90 minutes after the replayed final.

title: 45 days till Arizona Cardinals' opener: Remembering the 1945 season
description: With 45 days until the Arizona Cardinals' 2026 opener, let's look back at their 1945 season.
fullText:
We continue the countdown to the start of the Arizona Cardinals' regular season. Today, Thursday, July 30, is 45 days away from the Arizona Cardinals' regular-season opener on Sept. 13 on the road against the Los Angeles Chargers.

With 45 days until Week 1, let's look back at the 1945 season for the Cardinals.

The Cardinals were awful in 1945. They went 1-9 and were in last place. They were shut out four times, and they lost their final six games of the season. They averaged less than 10 points per game (9.8) and allowed 22.8.

In their four shutout losses, they failed to get even 10 first downs. They turned the ball over multiple times seven times.

Quarterback Paul Christman led the NFL with 219 passing attempts, but he completed only 40.9% of them for 1,147 yards, five touchdowns and 2 interceptions.

Frank Seno rushed for a team-high 355 yards and two touchdowns. Leo Cantor added 291 and rushed for a team-high five touchdowns.

Billy Dewell's 26 receptions led the team. He had 370 yards and one touchdown. Ed Rucinski caught 23 passes for a team-high 400 yards and two scores.

Cantor also led the defense with five interceptions.

Get more Cardinals and NFL coverage from Cards Wire's Jess Root and others by listening to the latest on the Rise Up, See Red podcast. Subscribe on Spotify, YouTube or Apple Podcasts.

title: 3 NBA players Heat should target in trades after losing out on LeBron sweepstakes
description: This is how the Miami Heat can regroup after losing out on LeBron James.
fullText:
The Miami Heat were a frontrunner in the LeBron sweepstakes, with many people around the NBA, including their social media team, believing James was going to sign there. Instead, Miami missed out on King James.

Miami knew that after making the blockbuster deal to acquire Giannis Antetokounmpo, it had to sign another notable free agent to become a contender in the Eastern Conference.

Since LeBron waited until the end of free agency to make his decision, there aren’t many options left for Miami. Still, there are three free agents the Heat could target to establish themselves as legitimate contenders.

MORE: 3 NBA teams who are most improved entering 2026-2027 season

DeRozan was released by the Sacramento Kings earlier this offseason, and he would likely be the best fit in Miami.

DeRozan is entering his 17th NBA season and proved last year that he still has plenty left in the tank. He averaged 18 points per game in 77 games. Miami is lacking significant guard play, with its projected starting backcourt consisting of Davion Mitchell and Tim Hardaway Jr. Those players aren’t bad, but on a championship contender they’re probably better suited as depth pieces.

DeRozan has a couple of options in free agency, with several teams scrambling to make a move after LeBron signed with Philadelphia.

The Los Angeles Clippers recently traded Kawhi Leonard, signaling the start of a rebuild, so they likely won’t re-sign Bradley Beal.

Beal played just six games last season, but when healthy, he’s still an elite scorer in the league. We’re only five years removed from Beal leading the NBA in scoring at 31 points per game. It’s clear Miami needs help in the backcourt, and he could take some of the offensive burden off Giannis and Bam Adebayo.

MORE: 3 NBA teams that have quietly won the offseason already

Though Bennedict Mathurin is a restricted free agent, rumors are circulating that the Clippers are looking for sign-and-trade partners.

Mathurin is entering his fifth season and has established himself as a reliable scorer. The young guard was traded to Los Angeles last year in a deal with the Indiana Pacers. He has consistently averaged around 17 points per game throughout his young career while making slight improvements in nearly every other statistical category. Mathurin is the youngest and most athletic option, but he would also be the most difficult player for the Heat to acquire.

If the Heat want to become true contenders, Mathurin might be their best option.

title: Eagles rookie QB Cole Payton is quietly turning heads at camp
description: The fifth-round rookie has become one of camp's early storylines.
fullText:
When the Philadelphia Eagles kicked off training camp this week in South Philly, most of the attention was expected to stay on Jalen Hurts adjusting to new offensive coordinator Sean Mannion, and the ongoing QB2 battle between Tanner McKee and Andy Dalton. Instead, rookie signal-caller Cole Payton has emerged as one of the early surprises of training camp.

After the first day of padded practice, reporters on hand couldn't help but notice Payton's arm talent.

Quez Watkins with a sick catch deep from Cole Payton. Nice throw as well.

— Eliot Shorr-Parks (@EliotShorrParks) July 29, 2026

ESPN's camp notes from Day 1 backed up the buzz, describing a deep throw where Payton connected with Britain Covey.

Rookie QB Cole Payton showed some really nice touch on deep throws, including one that he shot over defenders and into the arms of receiver Britain Covey down the right seam. He has impressed so far this offseason.

Philadelphia selected Payton in the fifth round (178th overall) of the 2026 NFL Draft out of North Dakota State, where he spent five seasons and became the full-time starter as a senior. In that lone year as the Bison's starter, Payton threw for 2,719 yards, 16 touchdowns, and just 4 interceptions while completing over 71% of his passes; numbers that helped him bring home a second FCS national championship. He's also no slouch as a runner, piling up 777 rushing yards and 13 rushing touchdowns that same season.

At 6-foot-3, 232 pounds, Payton profiles as more than just a clipboard-holder. His unique blend of arm strength and mobility has even sparked speculation about a broader offensive role down the line, though for now the focus remains squarely on quarterback development.

New Eagles QB Cole Payton —

• 6-foot-3, 233 pounds
• 16 passing TD, 13 rushing TD in 2025
• Hyper accurate, 72% comp. last year
• A LEFTY

Will be a fun preseason watch. pic.twitter.com/Zerq1zBncN

— Victor Williams (@ThePhillyPod) April 25, 2026

Payton currently projects as the fourth quarterback on Philadelphia's depth chart behind Hurts, McKee, and Dalton, and making the 53-man roster as a true fourth QB would be unusual for the franchise. An encouraging start to camp is exactly the kind of momentum a late-round rookie needs heading into preseason games.

title: More expected of Vandals after Day 1 of fall camp
description: Jul. 30—MOSCOW — The Vandals began Day 1 of their long journey into the 2026 football season with fall camp Wednesday. It was a practice full of shell drills, some seven-on-seven and a small amount of 11-on-11 on the outdoor practice field. But afterward, Idaho coach Thomas Ford Jr. sternly addressed his team, clarifying that to achieve what the Vandals want this season, the team will simply ...
fullText:
Jul. 30—MOSCOW — The Vandals began Day 1 of their long journey into the 2026 football season with fall camp Wednesday.

It was a practice full of shell drills, some seven-on-seven and a small amount of 11-on-11 on the outdoor practice field.

But afterward, Idaho coach Thomas Ford Jr. sternly addressed his team, clarifying that to achieve what the Vandals want this season, the team will simply have to put in more work.

"Like I said, 'Was today's practice bad?' 'No,' but I didn't think it was good enough for where we want to get to," Ford said in a post-practice news conference. "If we want to take this program to where we want to get back to, we have to do a little bit better job consistently with the way we practice, and not so much what we're doing, but just the way we're doing it."

To be completely frank, Day 1 of fall camp will not show exactly what a team will look like.

Overreactions to certain moments or issues can be easy to come by, but shouldn't be cause for concern.

Senior quarterback Joshua Wood said Day 1 was an opportunity to find the "little kinks" in the offense with first-year Vandals' offensive coordinator Ian Shoemaker and fix them up.

"It felt great," Wood said about working in the offense. "We felt there were a couple of explosive plays that had happened today. We're in Day 1 install, so a lot of Day 1 stuff that we're trying to get down and get the fine-tune things down."

Explosive plays — as Wood explained at the Big Sky Football Kickoff Weekend on Monday — will be a focus for the offense this season.

One of which included a nearly 40-yard touchdown to junior receiver Marquawn McCraney during an 11-on-11 portion.

Wood explained that the first day of installing the new offense is helpful in creating a good baseline in what to work off of.

"Day 1 is really what your base offense is," the quarterback said. "So just being able to get all that down and create some explosive plays, especially with not having the pads on and having spiders on. So being able to have explosive plays in the run game and then also in the pass game as well, and being able to just execute overall in general has been great."

Ford had a similar sentiment and said that there will be a focus on attention to detail.

"I think offensively, just cleaning up the small things, pre-snap things specifically, and we got to make sure that when we're open, we got to finish plays," Ford said. "Had a couple guys down the field open today; either we did not get it to (them), or they did not secure it. So we just need to do a much better job on the execution, especially offensively. Defensively, I thought we still need to continue to work on communication."

Going into Year 2 as a HC and players with more experience

On Monday, Ford said that he feels that this 2026 Vandals team feels more prepared because many of the players will be going into the season with hundreds of snaps to some with over a thousand snaps.

He reiterated that after Wednesday's practice.

"I think just seeing the amount of experience, especially on defense," Ford said. "I think just looking from last year, and you fast forward it to now, our secondary is light years ahead of where they were a year ago. I think the communication portion of defense is much improved from a year ago, but again, a lot of that comes with experience. Guys that have been in those situations, been in those practices, and so it was really nice to see that."

From Ford's perspective, he said the amount of organization and groundwork put in has given him a vastly different feeling than the beginning of last year.

"I feel like this year's preparation was not such a crash course," the second-year head coach said. "When you get a job in January, and you're hiring 17 coaches, and you're trying to get 30 or 40 guys out of the transfer portal, a lot of it is like drinking through a fire hose, and so I think this year just felt a lot more slowed down. Felt like we're much more prepared.

"Practice (is) really practice instead of 'Oh, what did we forget? What did we miss?' We didn't miss anything. So I think the preparation has just been so much better, and it makes it a lot easier for me, especially in practice."

A fresh face earns the 'Battle Axe'

Freshman linebacker Geovoney Burks earned the "Battle Axe" award for the best individual performance at the practice.

Burks said he arrived in Moscow just six weeks ago.

"It's crazy; the first two weeks, I say it was pretty hard to adjust," Burks said. "New playbook, new environment, but it's just I feel like I've been building week-by-week, each day, just getting better, and I'm blessed. I'm blessed to be here today."

To build on that, he said he plans to keep his "foot on the pedal" and attempt to get better each day.

He said to celebrate the award, his plan was to immediately call his family.

"I'm calling my mom, my sister, and my brother, and my grandma — all four of them," Burks said. "I'm making a group FaceTime call for all of them. Let them know."

title: Jake Paul’s fight promotion acquires UFC’s rivals to launch new MMA brand
description: MVP and PFL have merged, but with the new company operating under the MVP banner as Paul bids to disrupt the UFC’s hold on mixed martial arts
fullText:
Jake Paul’s company Most Valuable Promotions (MVP) has acquired the Professional Fighters League (PFL), with a new brand set to enter the world of mixed martial arts (MMA)

PFL was one of the few legitimate alternatives to the UFC, which is MMA’s flagship promotion, yet after recent executive exits the PFL has been acquired by MVP, which is known for its boxing shows but organised its first MMA event this year.

Paul, a YouTuber-turned-boxer, and his business partner Nakisa Bidarian put on MVP MMA 01 in May, with icons of the sport Ronda Rousey and Gina Carano headlining in Los Angeles.

Also on the card were former UFC fan favourites Nate Diaz and Mike Perry, and ex-UFC and PFL champion Francis Ngannou.

Perry beat Diaz via doctor stoppage after Ngannou knocked out Philipe Lins in the first round, and the evening ended with Rousey submitting Carano in 17 seconds.

While the event relied on older fighters (Rousey, 39, had not fought in 10 years, and Carano, 44, had not fought in 17), it was seen by many as refreshing for the sport, given the relative lack of top-level alternatives to the UFC.

Still, Paul and Bidarian had hinted at an uncertain future for MVP’s endeavours in MMA, with a maximum of a few shows per year. But that looks set to change due to the acquisition of the PFL, which should take full effect in 2027.

A press release on Thursday said: “PFL CEO John Martin will serve as CEO and board member, and lead the overall business of the combined company [...] Bidarian will continue to drive MVP’s boxing verticals and blockbuster live events, and work closely with Martin and the executive team. Paul, the world’s most-followed combat sports promoter, will continue leveraging his platform, audience, and cultural influence to drive audience growth, fighter development, brand expansion, and fan engagement across all areas of the business.”

The statement continued: “Together, MVP will feature nearly 400 elite athletes, including world champions, title contenders, and many of the biggest names across combat sports. The company intends to invest aggressively in both boxing and MMA.

“MVP and PFL will maintain relationships with many of the world's leading media and distribution partners, including Netflix, ESPN, Sky Sports, and PFL's extensive network of 34 partners across Europe, the Middle East, Africa, Asia, Latin America, and other key territories, including Brazil, Australia, and New Zealand.”

MVP MMA 01 streamed live on Netflix and reached an estimated audience of 17m viewers globally. The fight card achieved a peak of 11.6m viewers in the US, surpassing the previous MMA record of 8.8m set in 2011 by UFC on Fox 1.
